content.text:
I fixed it: in Node.js, axios now uses `timeoutErrorMessage` when a request times out, instead of always saying "timeout of Xms exceeded".

The Node.js request handler in `lib/adapters/http.js` had the default message hard-coded and never checked the config option. The browser version already handled it correctly, so I copied the same logic: use `config.timeoutErrorMessage` if it's set, otherwise keep the default message.

I checked it with a quick script against a local server that never responds. With `timeout: 100` and `timeoutErrorMessage: 'Custom'`, the request was rejected with the message `Custom` and code `ECONNABORTED`. I didn't run the existing test suite or add a test.
